title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Guardrails, Quantization & Regression Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This playbook codifies Redwood's end-to-end applied-ML evals process: how models are onboarded into the eval-harness, how prompt sets and benchmarks are created and versioned, required quality guardrails, quantization profile integration, and a prioritized regression triage process for escalations and rollbacks.
introduction: Purpose: Provide a single reference for cross-functional teams (Applied ML, Serving Runtime, Product, QA) that standardizes onboarding steps, evaluation expectations, and operational playbooks to detect, triage, and remediate model quality regressions introduced by model updates, prompt changes, or quantization. This document assumes familiarity with the eval-harness and the Redwood model catalog.
scope: This playbook covers: (1) eval-harness configuration and onboarding checklists; (2) prompt set and benchmark design, labeling conventions, and versioning; (3) quality guardrails and alerting thresholds; (4) quantization profile verification for inference; (5) regression triage and escalation playbook. It does NOT cover detailed infra runbook steps for provisioning GPUs (see eng-infra) or contract/legal reviews for customer-specific data (see security-and-compliance).
objectives:
- Reduce time-to-validated-serving for new models to < 5 business days for standard model families.
- Detect regressions before rollout with automated gates (unit test-level pass rates, prompt-set pass rates, quality delta limits).
- Provide clear ownership and SLAs for triage and rollback decisions.
- Ensure quantized variants maintain quality within defined tolerances for production use-cases.
roles_and_responsibilities:
- Applied ML (owner): authors eval suites, defines prompt sets and quality metrics, runs onboarding evals.
- Serving Runtime: provides performance profiles, quantization support, and kernel-level regressions guidance.
- Product: approves benchmark selection and business-critical prompts.
- SRE/Oncall: monitors aggregate user-facing quality metrics and triggers incident playbooks.
- Solutions/Customer Success: provides customer-specific prompt sets when requested and verifies for sensitive deployments.
eval_harness_guidelines:
1) Baseline configuration: every model must have an eval-harness config (.yaml) with: model_id, tokenizer, test_shards, deterministic_sampling_seed, and list of prompt_set_ids.
2) Unit-level tests: include 20-50 deterministic unit prompts that must pass verbatim to be considered 'build green'.
3) Metric family: for each prompt set declare metrics (exact_match_rate, semantic_similarity (embedding cosine), nlu_f1, hallucination_score) and thresholds.
4) CI integration: eval-harness jobs run on PRs for model adapters and on scheduled nightly regression jobs. Jobs must produce artifact bundle (jsonl) with seeds, outputs, and metric deltas.
5) Artifact retention: attach eval artifacts to model onboarding ticket and store in artifact-bucket with path convention: s3://redwood-evals/{model_id}/{version}/artifacts/{YYYY-MM-DD}/
prompt_sets_and_benchmarks:
Design Principles: prompts should reflect product intent, edge cases, and adversarial examples.
- Cataloging: prompt_set metadata must include: author, use_case, customer_impact (low/medium/high), expected_outputs, labels schema, and data provenance.
- Versioning: prompt_set ids use semantic versioning (e.g., customer-support-v1.2). Changes that alter expectations require major version bump and re-eval of dependent models.
- Benchmarks: create two tiers of benchmarks: Core (business-critical, ~200 prompts) and Exploratory (~1k prompts) used for stress/regression analysis.
- Labeling: ground-truth labels stored as JSONL with fields: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output, quality_tier, tags. Use manual review combined with crowd/QA for initial labeling and periodic audits (quarterly).
model_onboarding_process:
Checklist: 
1) Pre-onboarding: validate model license and artifacts, collect performance profile from serving-runtime team.
2) Create model entry in catalog with metadata (architecture, param_count, tokenizer, training_data_notes, initial_evals).
3) Run eval-harness against Core + Exploratory prompt sets. Record metrics and attach artifact bundle.
4) Quantization smoke tests (see quantization_profiles section).
5) If metrics meet thresholds, run canary deploy to Dedicated pool with traffic split 5%. Monitor user-facing metrics for 48 hours.
6) If stable, schedule ramp to 25% then 100% following rollback windows.
Required artifacts: onboarding ticket, eval artifact bundle, performance profile, security sign-off (if customer data used).
quality_guardrails:
Mandatory guardrails for all production models: 
- Absolute thresholds: Core exact_match_rate >= baseline - 1.5% AND semantic_similarity >= baseline - 0.02. 
- Relative delta gates: any PR/model update producing > 1.0% degradation on Core benchmark triggers automatic embargo until investigation.
- Hallucination guard: hallucination_score must not increase by > 10% relative to baseline.
- Behavioral tests: pass all product-critical unit tests.
- Monitoring: real-time sampling of user requests (1% sample) with automated heuristic checks (toxicity, hallucination heuristics) and daily human review for high-impact customers.
Alerting and dashboards: pre-built dashboards in Redwood Console for per-prompt-set pass rates, token-level drift, and model divergence heatmaps. Paging thresholds: severity-1 if Core pass rate drops > 2% or user-facing errors increase > 50%.
quantization_profiles:
Integration steps: 
1) Profile target model with representative sequence-length distribution and activation stats.
2) Apply recommended quantization profile (from quantization-profiles catalog) and run quantization smoke tests in eval-harness.
3) Required checks: token-level perplexity delta, Core benchmark metric delta, and end-to-end latency improvements.
4) Tolerances: for int8 and 4-bit variants, quality deltas on Core must be within configured tolerances (default: exact_match_rate delta <= 2.5%, semantic_similarity delta <= 0.04).
5) If tolerance breached, iterate on calibration (per-channel scaling, KL calibration) or fallback to higher-precision variant for specific routes.
Artifacts: save quantization profile yaml, calibration stats, and artifact bundle under s3://redwood-evals/quantized/{model_id}/{profile}/
regression_triage_playbook:
Purpose: Triage observed regressions post-deploy (automated or manual detection).
1) Detection: alerts from dashboards, CI failures, or customer reports. Log initial detection time, impacted model/version, and topline metric delta.
2) Triage (15-minute window): owner (Applied ML) runs quick checks: reproduce failing prompt(s) locally in eval-harness, compare raw outputs to baseline, and check for infra/perf anomalies.
3) Severity determination: Severity-1 (high) if Core pass rate drop > 2% or customer-impacting failures; Severity-2 (medium) if exploratory regressions or minor Core drifts.
4) Mitigation options: rollback to previous model version; apply temporary routing policy (route traffic to non-quantized variant); deploy fix patch to tokenizer or prompt normalization.
5) Postmortem: within 72 hours for S1 incidents publish incident report with RCA, timeline, mitigations, and action items.
6) Long-term controls: update prompt sets, add unit tests to eval-harness, or strengthen guardrail thresholds.
runbook_and_escalation:
Escalation flow: Applied ML -> Serving Runtime -> SRE -> Product -> Legal (if customer data implicated). SLA targets: initial triage within 15 minutes for S1, mitigation decision within 2 hours. Runbook snippets: commands to re-run eval-harness locally, sample CLI: 
- python -m eval_harness.run --model-id <id> --prompt-set core-v1 --seed 42 --output artifacts.jsonl
- aws s3 cp artifacts.jsonl s3://redwood-evals/{model}/{version}/artifacts/
metrics_and_monitoring: Key metrics to expose in Redwood Console: Core pass rate (1h/24h), delta vs baseline, token-level latency p50/p95, hallucination index, toxicity rate, user error rate. Set rolling-window anomaly detection and attach slack alerts to applied-ml-alerts channel. Include automated daily digest summarizing top failing prompts and quantization regressions.
